Terespol Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Terespol, Poland

Demolished. Despite an official 'demolished' classification and a narrative describing total destruction, this cemetery's preservation-condition category is listed as 'fenced and protected' — a mismatch worth flagging rather than resolving. Terespol itself was founded in 1697 in the village of Błotkowo, where Jews had already run an inn since the 16th century; in the 1850s, Russian authorities relocated the entire town several kilometers west to make way for a military fortress at Brześć, though this cemetery — founded in the mid-18th century and used until a new cemetery opened in 1858 — was not affected by that move. The Jewish population peaked at 85 percent of the town by 1907. The cemetery was partially destroyed during WWII, and in 1970 its remaining tombstones were removed and the land divided into house plots; nothing survives today.
